units.text: I have something concrete for the table: last night I followed player_3 and they targeted me — me specifically, player_4. That doesn't confirm a role, since healer, sentinel, trailseer, sigilist and chanteuse all target a player, but I'd like player_3 to say up front what they did to me, so I can check it against what I saw rather than everything they say after hearing this.

Night 1 follow on player_3 shows they visited me (player_4) — consistent with healer/watch/follow/sigil/block, so it's evidence not a verdict. Tonight I should follow a suspected Illusionist/Necromancer candidate rather than lock onto p3. Keep hidden; only reveal my track if p3 turns out to be a wolf carrier or I need to break a tie in claims. Watch the day's claims to cross-check: anyone claiming healer who protected me fits p3, but p3 hasn't spoken yet, so my follow stays private until I see who claims what.

player_3, I've got you visiting me last night. That doesn't mean anything bad — a healer or a sigil placement would look identical — but I want to hear what you were doing on me before I trust you. If your story is straight, we both learn something.

Day 2: my follow on player_3 (targeted me night 1) is thin evidence — any of several roles could visit a player. Best use of it: ask player_3 publicly to account for targeting me, and see if their story matches. Keep my role hidden for now unless I get a real smear or need to force a claim. If player_3 can't plausibly explain the visit, that's my vote; otherwise pick a follow target whose claim later needs checking.

Someone moved on me last night. player_3, I tracked you on night 1 and you targeted me. That's not a death sentence — you could have been the healer saving me — but nothing was attacked last night except player_1, so I want to hear what you actually did and why me. If you claim healer, that's checkable later by who shows up saved.

Day 2: I have one genuine result — night 1 player_3 targeted me. Nothing died night 1 except player_1 who was sigil-struck, so no attack is proven. I'll put this on the table as a claim (trailseer, target player_3) to force a response and generate data, without revealing the track is my role necessarily — actually it's fine as I have only 8 players alive and need conversation going. From tonight I track whoever behaves most suspiciously or fails to explain a visit. Cross-check any follow of a carrier against a morning wolf kill (illusionist hiding the trace is a gap to remember). Do not die with unused info: if I'm likely targeted, breadcrumb results in will.

I have a night result worth airing, because it's checkable: someone targeted me on night 1 and I want to hear them explain it before I say who. I'd rather you volunteer what you did on night 1 than have me call it out — that tells me more about you than the action itself. If nobody owns up, I'll name the player and we can question it then.

Night 1 follow shows player_3 targeting me — could be healer protect, Chanteuse block (Chanteuse is dead though, so no), or Sigilist/Vigilante. Since Chanteuse is dead, player_3's visit to me is most likely a Healer protect or a Vigilante's check/no-action, or a Sigilist placing a sigil on me. If a sigil was placed on me it'd have struck if I attacked — I targeted no one in attack, so no effect. I'll open with a soft claim framing to build trust and see how player_3 reacts. Keep precise role hidden; only reveal Trailseer if it becomes necessary to force accountability. Tonight follow someone whose claims look inconsistent or who stays silent.

I'll put my night 1 result on the table since it's the only concrete sighting we have: I tracked player_3 and player_3 targeted me. That's not a verdict - a Healer or Sigilist visit looks like that too - but with the Chanteuse dying to a sigil, someone out there attacked, so I want to hear what player_3 was doing on me. If you claim Healer or Sigilist, say who you targeted and why me.

Trailseer, alive. Night 1 tracked player_3 -> targeted me. That fits Sigilist/Healer protection but is odd for a healer to protect an unknown on N1, and the chanteuse died to a sigil (someone attacked player_1). Ambiguous; a wolf carrier could have been blocked or just seen night 2. I'll share it as a claim to prod player_3 for their story instead of burning a hold. Night 2: follow whoever's story contradicts, or a top suspicion; watch for wolf carrier visiting the death.

player_4, here's the thing you keep skipping: I'm the one with a result on you, and it says nobody targeted you last night — and since you're alive and unannounced, nothing that touched you could have been hidden. So 'player_3 visited player_4' isn't a wording slip, it's a result that can't exist. Where did it come from?

player_4's 'follow' story is impossible from my side: I watched player_4 night 1 and saw no one target them — and since player_4 survived unhidden, nothing targeting them could be concealed. I'll say it once more with that reason (survival means no concealment) rather than just denying. Don't reveal Sentinel unless the table is about to vote me out; offer my remaining watch as the day's direction instead. Tonight watch player_5 or player_6 to test the claimed check/heal.

Straight answer, player_4: no follow was needed to disprove you. I did visit no one on night 1 — but more to the point, a follow on me would have shown my destination, and you said \"player_3 visited player_4,\" meaning your own door. You don't get that wording from a follow on me. So which ability, on which target, actually produced that result?

player_4 is caught: my night-1 watch showed nobody targeting player_4, so their 'player_3 visited player_4' follow is fabricated — they never actually targeted me. I'll say so plainly without naming Sentinel yet, but the contradiction is exact and I should press it hard since it's the strongest evidence on the board. Wolves killed no one, so the pack's target was the Necromancer; that matters more later. Tonight's one remaining watch should go on a claimed power role (player_5 or player_6) to test their stories.

Which is it? It's invented. I'm the Sentinel, and I watched player_4 last night — no one targeted them, so there was no visit at their door, mine or anyone's. A real follow showing me arriving at player_4 is impossible against that. Cast a vote on player_4 and stop entertaining the 'wording' angle.

My watch of player_4 night 1 showed no visitors, which directly kills their follow claim — I'll reveal that as the Sentinel now rather than keep arguing wording, because it makes the case airtight and player_3 is being squeezed by player_10's frame. Expect a counterattack; note who piles on player_4 vs. who tries to redirect to me. Save my last watch for a claimed power role (player_5 or player_6) tonight, not for player_4.

player_4, I'll answer it plainly: I visited nobody on night 1, and there's a hard reason I can say that with certainty, not just denial. Nobody came to your door last night — that's my own night result, and it's the opposite of the one you're quoting. So the question isn't what I did at your door; it's why you invented a visitor for it.

player_4's follow story is flatly contradicted by my night-1 watch on them: nobody targeted player_4, so no one visited them, and their 'player_3 visited player_4' result is invented. I'll press that contradiction hard without naming Sentinel yet, but if they keep doubling down I'll reveal the watch to lock the vote. player_1 (Chanteuse) carried the night-1 kill, so player_4 and the surviving Illusionist are what's left. Tonight's watch (1 left) goes on a claimed power role — player_6 if they survive.

player_4, I never visited you — and there's a way to settle it. Your result would still show if it were true, so I'll say plainly: someone was at my door would be visible to me. Since nothing was, either your follow is invented or it's smoke. I'm voting player_4 today; pull it if you have a real result.

player_4's trailseer story is disproven by my own watch: nobody targeted player_4 night 1, so 'player_3 visited player_4' cannot be true. I'll hold that line and push the vote onto player_4 rather than reveal the Sentinel. Keep watching a claimed power role (player_5 or player_6) tonight with my last watch.

The night-2 visit to player_7 matters most: player_2, player_5 and player_10 all targeted them. Player_5 was the healer doing the save and player_2 was the Illusionist, which leaves player_10 as the third visitor with no explained action. Player_10, what did you do to player_7 that night? That's where I'd vote right now.

I have no watches left, so my strength now is the night-2 watch: player_2, player_5 and player_10 all targeted player_7, with player_5 confirmed as the healer and player_2 revealed as the Illusionist carrier. That makes player_10 very likely the Chanteuse (or at least a wolf role) - I should push player_10 hard today, using the watch result only if I must. The Necromancer is among 1/6/8/9 and player_4's hidden body could be the other wolf. Priority vote: player_10.

The real unaddressed contradiction is player_7 vs player_8: one of them is lying about when the check on player_8 happened. If player_8's night-1 claim is true, player_7's whole read list is fabricated. I'd want player_10 to explain why they were on player_7 night 2, since more than one visitor showed up there and only the kill and the save are accounted for.

I have zero watches left, so I'm now just a town vote with private knowledge. My night-2 watch put player_2, player_5 and player_10 on player_7: player_2 was the Illusionist, player_5 the healer (now dead), which leaves player_10 as the remaining visitor — either a town role that targeted player_7 or the other attacker. Player_4's hidden body could be the Chanteuse, and the Necromancer is among player_1, player_6, player_8, player_9. I should push the contradiction between player_7 and player_8, and use my watch data on player_10 as leverage without revealing I'm the sentinel.

Two things I want on the record before the vote. First, player_7: you say you checked player_10 night 1 and player_8 night 2, but player_8 says they were checked night 1. One of you is wrong about which night — which is it, player_8? Second, player_10, what did you do on night 2? Just say it plainly.

No watches left, so I'm pure talk now. Night-2 watch showed player_2, player_5 and player_10 all targeting player_7; player_2 is dead (Illusionist), so the surviving wolf-side Chanteuse is likely player_10 or in player_4's hidden body. Player_10 is also the one player_7's claimed clean check restricts hardest — pressure them. The player_7 vs player_8 night-1 check dispute is the other testable contradiction; one of them lied. Vote direction: player_10 unless something breaks.

Naming who targeted whom on night 2: I had eyes on player_7, and the people who targeted them were player_2, player_5 and player_10. player_5 is the confirmed healer and player_2 was the Illusionist, so player_10 is the one who attacked player_7 that night. I'll say where that comes from if it's contested, but player_10 should explain what they were doing on player_7 first.

No watches left, so my role is spent; I'll only claim it if it can settle a dispute. Key facts: player_2, player_5, player_10 all targeted player_7 night 2; player_5 is confirmed healer, player_2 was the Illusionist, so player_10 is almost certainly the wolf who attacked player_7 that night — I should say that naming who targeted whom is a claim I can back, without yet dumping the role. Player_4's body was killed by a reanimated wolf and its role was hidden by a reanimated Illusionist, so the Necromancer is active with player_2's body. Today's likely move: pressure player_10 and see who defends them; vote player_10 unless something contradicts.

Fresh fact: night 2 I watched player_7 and saw player_2, player_5 and player_10 target them. player_5 is the healer (confirmed save), player_2 was the wolf, so player_10 needs to explain what they were doing on player_7 that night. I'm the Sentinel — that's my claim, one watch used, one used on player_4 night 1.

My night-2 watch on player_7 is a real fact I have not shared: player_2 (illusionist), player_5 (healer) and player_10 all targeted player_7 that night. Player_2 was the wolf attacker, player_5 the healer, which makes player_10's visit the most odd — unless player_10 is a town role that targeted player_7. Tonight player_4's body is available to the Necromancer, so player_4's hidden role matters. I have 0 watches left, so I must convert to a spoken claim to get any value; share the night-2 watch once the table starts picking a lynch. My vote priority: a player contradicting night-2 visit facts, likely player_10.

player_8, you keep saying player_7 checked you on night 1. I have a sighting that player_7 visited someone on night 2, not night 1, and did nothing at all last night. If you're clean you should be able to say exactly which night player_7's visit to you happened — a real investigator's target usually remembers the night they were checked.

Night 3 track on player_7 showed no target, which is consistent with a check on the dead player_5 (held/no visit) and rules out player_7 being the wolf carrier that night. That makes player_7 a poor lynch and a decent bet as investigator, so player_8's night-1 contradiction is the sharper thread. I should press player_8 on exactly whom they claim player_7 targeted on night 1, since my night-2 track proves the player_8 visit happened night 2. Hold my trailseer results back unless someone pushes a fake investigator claim that my track can break.

player_7, you told us the last check was going on player_5 night 3. What did it actually read, and why should we trust it when your night-1 and night-2 accounts already conflict with player_8? If that check was never made, say so now rather than later — that's the difference between a sloppy claim and a lie.

Player_7 on night 3 targeted no one — that contradicts their announced plan to check player_5, so their investigator claim just got shakier, but I can't reveal the track without outing myself. So I'll press player_7 for their actual night-3 result/plan directly and see if the story holds; if the table starts moving on player_7 I can follow with the track. Player_8 remains secondary suspicion. Push the lynch on player_7 unless they produce something testable.

player_7 — did the night-3 check on player_5 actually happen? A check on a town healer would read Not suspicious anyway, so the useful thing isn't the target, it's whether you were blocked or held. If you got 'roleblocked' that names a living Chanteuse and someone to look at; if you held, say so plainly. That's the one unresolved thread from last night.

Night 3 follow of player_7 shows it targeted no one, contradicting its announced-but-unstated plan to check player_5. That's not proof of lying (it may have held, or been blocked by the Chanteuse), but the vanished check needs explaining. The real uninvestigated danger is the Necromancer plus one living Chanteuse — with player_2's body usable, a reanimated wolf attack is the biggest threat. Push player_7 for the night-3 check outcome, keep my role hidden, and read player_8's push on player_7 against the vote record.

player_7 said they'd check player_5 on night 3. I followed player_7 last night and they targeted nobody. Either that check never happened or player_7 got blocked — and player_5, who would have been the test, is dead. That's worth an explanation, player_7.

Night 3 track on player_7 showed no targeting, so player_7's claimed check on player_5 probably never happened — either blocked or the claim is false. That's a real contradiction to raise. I'm the trailseer; I can prove my track claim by naming nights 2 and 3 results. Keep leaning on player_8's conflicting night-1 check story. Next night I should track someone who isn't a likely night kill: player_8 or player_6.

player_7, you told the table your last check would go on player_5 on night 3 — and the player_5 check can never happen now, so I want to know why the planned action didn't occur. Did you get roleblocked, or did you actually hold? That's the most testable lead left today, and nobody's touched it.

Night-3 result: player_7 targeted no one, so its promised check on player_5 never happened — yet its night-2 visit to player_8 checks out. That's the strongest open item today. With the healer and illusionist dead, the wolves and Necromancer both still act; no one died last night, which hints at protections/sigils or a hidden role's protection. Keep the trailseer role quiet; press player_7 on the missing check, and watch player_8's story about when it was checked.

I'm the trailseer, and I'll put my night-4 result out there: I followed player_1 and they targeted player_3 — the guy the wolves killed. That doesn't prove culpability by itself, but I want to hear what player_1 says they were doing visiting a dying Sentinel.

I'm the trailseer: night 1 player_9 no visit, night 2 player_7 visited player_8, night 3 player_7 no visit, night 4 player_1 visited player_3 (who died to wolves). I've claimed my results openly. With four alive and the record showing wolves plus a necromancer, I need to push for lynching one of player_1/player_6 rather than risk abstaining again — the town can't win a night war. player_8 is the one I'd trust most (two clean checks).

I'm the Trailseer. Night 4 I followed player_1: player_1 targeted player_3, and player_3 died to the wolves. The rules say the Necromancer only targets under a dead body's name and the Speculator never targets anyone, so player_1 is neither — which leaves wolf, or town role with an answer to give. player_1, what did you do to player_3?

Claim trailseer openly now: I'm otherwise a no-claim with weak standing and my night 4 follow is the key evidence. player_1 targeted player_3 last night — that's a real fact worth putting on the record. Night 1/2/3 results are already public claims via player_3's blunder (they named my visit), so no new exposure. Push hard at player_1 to explain the visit; then sort player_6 vs player_8 for Necromancer.

I'm the Trailseer. Last night I followed player_1 and they targeted player_3 — the player the wolves killed. player_1, what were you doing on player_3? A visit to the corpse is hard to explain away, so give us the action and its result. If it was a block or a kill-participation, that's you or the Chanteuse seat.

Last night I tracked player_1 targeting player_3 (the kill victim), and worked-out says player_1 is not the Necromancer or Speculator — so player_1 is either the Chanteuse (carried or blocked someone) or a town power carrying a targeting action on the death victim, both worth raising. I've already claimed Trailseer publicly and my night-2 follow of player_7 is corroborated by player_3's watch, so my credibility is decent; today I push player_1 to name their action on player_3. Player_6 vs player_8 is the Necromancer slot; player_6's total silence all game is the bigger flag. I want the vote on player_1 or player_6 and will argue from the visit evidence, not tone.

I've been holding this back but it needs saying now: I'm the Trailseer, and last night I followed player_1 — they targeted player_3, who was killed by the wolves that same night. That's a claim I can put to the Sentinel-type check or the Healer's record; someone at the table can verify the visitor pattern. player_8 is the other half: my reads and the roster narrow them to a killer role, and player_7's night-2 visit to player_8, which I saw myself, is the only confirmed trace linking a survivor to anything. I'd vote player_8 right now unless someone gives me a reason the night-4 visit from player_1 is benign.

Confirmed night-4 follow: player_1 targeted player_3, the night player_3 died (wolves' kill came through a body trace separately — actually player_3's death announced as 'killed by the wolves', which a Necromancer body would not be). So player_1's visit to player_3 is likely a block or a Sigil, not the wolf kill; still worth pressing. My containment: player_8 is narrowed to Vig/Sig/Necro/Spec since I hold Trailseer, so they're a strong vote. I should not name my role outright unless needed to explain my follow — but the follow IS the evidence, so I'll present it as tracking.

I've been quiet, so let me put one concrete thread on the table. Last night player_3 died to the wolves — I'd like whoever visited player_3 to say so before we vote, because I have reason to believe someone did. player_1, what did you do last night? An honest answer narrows this down fast; a dodge doesn't.

Still Trailseer. Key new fact: night 4 I followed player_1 and they targeted player_3, who died to the wolves that night — and the game confirms player_1 is neither Necromancer nor Speculator. So player_1 either carried the wolf kill or did something else to the victim; I should press player_1 to explain that visit publicly without tipping that I'm the one who saw it, and use it to steer today's vote. Remaining scum among player_1, player_6, player_8 (one chanteuse-type wolf, one Necromancer), so I want to force claims that narrow it. Keep my track hidden unless I need to spend it as leverage.

I'm the Trailseer, and I'll put my follows on record: night 2 I followed player_7 to player_8, night 3 player_7 went nowhere, night 4 player_1 went to player_3, and last night I followed player_6 — they went nowhere. That last one fits a Necromancer using a body under a dead name, since a body's visit would still read as player_6 targeting someone. Both wolves are dead, so it's player_6 or player_8 — player_6, you've claimed nothing all game; what were you doing on nights 3 and 4?

I'm the Trailseer; both wolves are dead, so tonight's threat is the Necromancer, which is player_6 or player_8. I claim my role now and put my follows on record: they confirm player_7 targeted player_8 (night 2) and nobody (night 3), and player_1 targeted player_3 (night 4) — matching the dead wills' stories. Since we're down to 3 players with the Necromancer killing at night, we must vote today; player_6's total silence on role makes them my default, but I'll weigh player_8's answer. Voting player_6 if nothing changes.

Time to close this out — both wolves are dead, so one of player_6 or player_8 is the Necromancer. I'm the Trailseer and my follows have checked out: I tracked player_1 onto player_3 on night 4, matching player_3's last night, and last night I followed player_6, who targeted no one. That's not a defence — the Necromancer can just hold the body. player_6, you've made no role claim all game; which role are you, and why did you hold last night?

Three players left: me (Trailseer), player_6, player_8. Both wolves are dead, so the Necromancer is one of them. I should reveal the one thing only I know that narrows it: my night-5 follow on player_6 showed no target, and my tracks have matched player_3's watch and player_7's claims. Push the two of them to name a role; player_6 has never claimed, which is the weakest position. Aim the vote at whichever of player_6/player_8 cannot account for the casting.

Here's the arithmetic: both wolves are dead, so player_6 and player_8 are the only bodies left besides me, and exactly one of them is the Necromancer. That means we don't need a clever solve — we lynch one today and the other tomorrow if needed. My only result to offer that matters: I followed player_6 last night and they targeted no one, which fits someone doing nothing or acting through a dead body, so it proves nothing either way. player_6, you've named no role and no night actions at all while player_8 at least claims Sigilist — give me a night-by-night account now.

Vote math is the whole story now: player_6 and player_8 are the only non-me survivors, both wolves are dead, so exactly one is the Necromancer. Any eliminations today and tomorrow cleanly settle it either way; abstaining (if offered) just wastes a day. My night-5 follow on player_6 showed no visit, but a Necromancer can skip a night or just protect/block through a body, so silence isn't exculpatory. I'll press player_6 for any role claim and a specific night-by-night account, since player_8 has at least given a claim.

I'm the trailseer. Last night I followed player_6 and they targeted no one — but a necromancer who holds is invisible to a track, so that settles nothing by itself. player_6, you've made no role claim all game; which role are you, and did you ever use a dead body?

Both wolves are dead; only the Necromancer remains and it is player_6 or player_8. My track of player_6 last night showed them targeting no one, which is evidence but not proof — the Necromancer may simply have held. Today I should press player_6 directly: did they act through a body on any night, and if not, why sit on the one ability that could win them the game. The vote should go to whichever of the two can't explain their nights; currently leaning player_6.

Let's not waste the day on vibes — there's one threat left, the Necromancer, and it's player_6 or player_8. I'll commit to following one of you tonight, so tell me now: which body would you use and on whom? A Necromancer who claims a target and then shows up under a dead name on my track is caught, and one who claims nothing has to explain why.

Both wolves dead; the only live threat is the Necromancer, so today's lynch must hit player_6 or player_8. My night-5 follow showed player_6 targeted no one, which is neutral (they could have held the body ability), so I can't lean on it alone. The cleaner tell: if player_6 or player_8 could use a dead body and chose not to, ask them to commit to a target and I will follow that player tonight to test the promise. Vote the one who can't explain their nights; I lean player_6 for zero claims.

I'll put my night result on the table since day 1 gave us nothing else: I tracked player_6 and they targeted player_7. Sentinel fits — player_6 likely watched you, player_7. If so, did you learn anything, and did anyone get attacked but saved? That's the only lead we have right now.

Track result: player_6 targeted player_7 on night 1. Sentinels watch, so player_6 likely watched player_7 — meaning player_7 was probably attacked by wolves or SK, but player_6 also could have been a wolf-carrier variant? No, player_6 was town sentinel. So player_7 got targeted by player_6's watch. If wolves or SK targeted player_7 and it died (healer saved), we'd know, but night report showed only two deaths. Possibility: player_7 was the wolves' kill target and was saved (announced as saved), but no save announced. Or player_6 watched player_7 and saw nothing/wolf-kill hidden. Actually player_6 could have been wolves' kill if they carried? No — sentinel is town. So the wolves killed player_6, meaning player_6 was their kill target and the SK killed player_6 too? Both kills on player_6? Actually SK 'stabbed' player_6 — SK kills. Wolves killed player_10. So player_6 targeted player_7 with his watch. That's the only data. Nothing conclusive about player_7. Decided to share softly: state I tracked and saw player_6 target player_7, framed to prompt claims. Keep watching next target on someone who hasn't claimed.

I've got something concrete: player_6, our sentinel, targeted player_7 on night 1 before dying. Sentinels watch; they don't attack. So player_7, what did you get up to that made the sentinel look at you — did anyone target you last night? That's the one lead we have, and I'd rather chase it than guess at quiet people.

Night 1 result: player_6 (sentinel) targeted player_7, and player_6 died to the serial killer. Player_7 is the one clean lead — ask what they know about being targeted. Keep trailseer concealed for now; reveal only if I catch a killer carrier, and only if it buys me real credibility. Night 2: track someone likely to act offensively (a claimed-role hub or a suspicious speaker) rather than a dead end. Two deaths a night (wolves + SK) means the town is bleeding fast — push for an elimination today, not an abstain.

Two kills on night 1 means the SK and wolves both acted, so anyone who tries to sell a clean story about last night is reaching. One thing worth flagging: player_7 has drawn a night visit from someone already, so their account of their own night matters. What did you do last night, player_7?

I'm the trailseer; my only result is that player_6 targeted player_7 on night 1, but player_6 was the sentinel and died to the SK — so that targeting is likely the sentinel's watch, not an attack, weakening its value as a wolf tell. I should not reveal my role for that thin result, since it would paint a target on my back. Today I'll use the floor to note player_7 is worth scrutinizing but not accuse blindly; the SK and wolves both struck night 1, so tonight choose a target carefully and only soft-claim if I catch a genuine carrier/SK trace.

Heads up on night 1: the sentinel player_6 was targeting someone that night, and my read says the Sentinel is gone. Nobody's said a word today, so I've got nothing solid yet — but I'd rather say that than invent suspicion. Before we vote, let's each at least state what we did or held night 1, so blanks are answerable.

Night 1 track: player_6 (the dead sentinel) targeted player_7 — so player_7 had a visitor (player_6), which is worth noting but not guilt. Sentinel and Healer are gone, so town is thin; the real threats are wolves (Chanteuse/Illusionist) and the Serial Killer. Don't hard-claim Trailseer yet; my track result on player_6->player_7 is soft info. Tonight follow someone likely to act (a claimed investigator or the suspicious one). Watch who pushes with no evidence — that's a wolf/SK tell. If I get a strong track (someone visiting the wolf kill), soft-claim then.

Player_6 was the sentinel, and I tracked them last night — they targeted player_7. That's a fact you can all test against whatever player_7 says they did. A sentinel visiting someone on night 1 is worth explaining, so player_7, what's your story?",

Day 1 was silent, so I have no behavioral reads. My night 1 track shows player_6 (sentinel, now dead) targeted player_7 — worth a soft claim to generate discussion, since a sentinel visiting someone is odd and the info has no downside now that player_6 is dead. Keep watching who claims results and whether any claim contradicts player_7's story. Hold my second check/track for a clearer target, and lean toward voting on the player whose claims conflict with verifiable facts.

The three people who voted player_4 yesterday were 7, 8 and 9 — and player_4 turned out to be the chanteuse. That bloc bothers me, but 9 is dead, so we can't read their info. Who among the survivors actually has a night result worth sharing today? Staying silent just helps the serial killer and illusionist hide.
